assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical lattice clocks are a textbook measurement advance: neutral atoms trapped at the magic wavelength give fractional uncertainties and stabilities near 1e-18, which opens redefinition of the second, relativistic geodesy and tests of fundamental constants. The idea (Katori, 2001-2003) was followed by decisive experimental demonstrations, and the field has been opened to many groups. This is exactly the kind of precision-measurement instrument that changes what can be observed.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed the magic-wavelength lattice concept and made the first demonstrations; Ye's group drove the strontium clock to record accuracy and stability and linked it to ultrastable lasers and quantum-many-body physics. The two-person configuration is clean and credit appears reasonably settled, though Ye's frequency-comb and laser-stabilization work sits partly in territory already recognized in 2005.
assessment.maturity: Multiple independent labs (JILA, RIKEN/Tokyo, PTB, NIST, SYRTE, others) have confirmed and surpassed performance, and clock comparisons are routine. Timely and mature; the formal SI redefinition is still pending but this does not weaken the physics.
uncertainties: The exact division between Katori's concept and Ye's later performance leadership is a judgment call, and I am not independently verifying priority details.
Overlap with the 2005 prize for the frequency comb could be raised by colleagues.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Ultracold atoms in optical lattices turned the Hubbard model into a laboratory instrument: the Mott-insulator transition, single-site-resolved quantum gas microscopy, and programmable many-body Hamiltonians. The impact reaches condensed-matter, quantum information and measurement of correlations at a level that is hard to access in solids.
assessment.attribution: Zoller (with Jaksch, Cirac and others) supplied the theoretical blueprint; Greiner and Bloch executed the Mott transition and microscope work experimentally. I would choose one theorist and two experimentalists; Cirac would be equally defensible in place of Zoller, but Cirac and Zoller are also credited on other entries and I prefer not to double count.
assessment.maturity: Highly mature, replicated by dozens of groups, and now used as quantum simulators. The field was partly recognized by 2001 (BEC) and 2012 (Haroche, Wineland), so the prize must be framed carefully around lattice simulation.
uncertainties: Who among Greiner, Bloch, Zoller, and Cirac has the strongest claim is contested within the community.
Four credited names for a three-person limit forces omissions that may look arbitrary.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Single colour-centre spins, most prominently the nitrogen-vacancy centre in diamond, gave optical readout and coherent control of single solid-state spins at room temperature. This led to nanoscale magnetometry, thermometry and biological sensing, as well as quantum registers and networks. Both fundamental and with direct measurement impact, which fits my own emphasis on new ways to observe nature.
assessment.attribution: Wrachtrup and Jelezko made the first optical detection and coherent control of a single NV spin; Awschalom's group broadened the platform across defects (including SiC) and to ultrafast control. Lukin is credited here but his decisive role is more tied to the quantum-optics and Rydberg proposals, and I keep him for B008.
assessment.maturity: Well confirmed by many independent groups and moving into commercial sensing, but some applications (in vivo sensing, quantum networks) are still evolving. Recognition is reasonable now, not premature.
uncertainties: Attribution across Awschalom, Jelezko, Wrachtrup and Lukin is not clean, and the early NV literature involves further people not on this list.
I cannot verify exact first-demonstration dates from memory.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Programmable Rydberg atom arrays combine optical tweezers with blockade interactions to give hundreds of individually controlled qubits, high-fidelity entangling gates and large-scale analogue quantum simulation of exotic phases. A strong demonstration-driven platform with experimental evidence for coherence and control.
assessment.attribution: Saffman contributed early Rydberg-gate proposals and demonstrations; Browaeys and Lukin led the tweezer-array many-body experiments. The set is plausible, though Weiss, Bernien/Endres, and others would be relevant and are not listed.
assessment.maturity: Rapidly maturing; independent groups (Harvard/QuEra, Paris, Caltech, Wisconsin, others) reproduce key results, but the long-term outcome for quantum computing is still open, so this is somewhat early.
uncertainties: Timing could be premature relative to older candidates in the same field.
Several important contributors are absent from the supplied credit list.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Circuit QED made strong coupling of a single microwave photon to a superconducting qubit routine, with dispersive readout and the architecture used in essentially all leading superconducting processors. The experimental recipes (coherence, readout, control) are the working tools of the field.
assessment.attribution: Blais supplied the theory proposal with Huang, Wallraff, Girvin and Schoelkopf; Wallraff and Schoelkopf delivered the 2004 strong-coupling experiment. Girvin is an important theorist not on this list, and the 2025 prize on macroscopic quantum tunnelling in circuits complicates framing.
assessment.maturity: Highly replicated and technologically impactful. The recent 2025 prize in a neighbouring area suggests the committee may wish to wait, though that is a strategy question and not a scientific one.
uncertainties: Overlap with the recent circuit-quantum prize may reduce near-term priority.
Girvin's absence from the credited names leaves a likely attribution gap.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The qPlus tuning-fork AFM with CO-functionalized tips gives real-space images of molecular bond structure and charge distribution at sub-atomic resolution. A genuine instrumentation advance that opened new observation of matter, in the spirit of my interest in measurement.
assessment.attribution: Giessibl invented the qPlus sensor; Gross and Meyer (IBM Zurich) demonstrated CO-tip bond-resolved imaging. The three-person configuration is natural, with Gimzewski/Binnig heritage in the background.
assessment.maturity: The technique is confirmed and widely adopted, but the impact outside surface science and chemistry is moderate so far, and the Nobel precedent for scanning probes (1986) raises the bar.
uncertainties: Breadth of impact on physics at large may be judged less than the quantum-technology candidates.
Possible competing claims for the CO-tip imaging contribution.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Pulsar-timing arrays detected the nanohertz gravitational-wave background through very precise timing, a remarkable measurement achievement that opens a new gravitational-wave band. Evidence emerged in 2023 from several collaborations.
assessment.attribution: Credit is the main difficulty: the result is the product of NANOGrav, EPTA, PPTA, InPTA and CPTA, with decades of work by many people, and three names cannot capture it fairly.
assessment.maturity: Evidence is at roughly the 3-4 sigma level and independent confirmation and source identification (supermassive black hole binaries versus other origins) are still pending, so this looks premature.
uncertainties: Significance and interpretation are not settled.
Attribution is hard to assign to three people.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Solid-state femtosecond lasers (Ti:sapphire, Kerr-lens mode-locking, and semiconductor saturable-absorber mirrors) made ultrafast lasers compact and reliable and underlie combs, attosecond science and imaging. The work comes from my own laser-physics tradition, and its impact on measurement is extensive.
assessment.attribution: Moulton developed Ti:sapphire as a laser medium, Sibbett's group demonstrated Kerr-lens mode locking, and Keller invented the SESAM and extended it to high-power modelocked lasers. The configuration is plausible but I admit it is a more technology-leaning set.
assessment.maturity: Very mature; the underlying technology is ubiquitous. Parts of the field were recognized in 2018 (CPA) and 2005 (combs), which makes a fresh prize harder to justify.
uncertainties: Overlap with earlier prizes in ultrafast optics.
Priority between Kerr-lens mode locking contributors (Sibbett, Spence, Ippen and others) is not fully reflected in the credited list.
